root_idea.summary: The root is oriented around the rear or nape and following what lies behind it: tracking, pursuit, and succession.
root_idea.development: From the nape and the act of following a trace, the usage develops into pursuing a matter, causing one thing to come after another, and related derivatives for poetic endings and attentive provision.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The inflected Quranic imperfect is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form قَفَا.
The inflected Quranic Form II verb is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form قَفَّى.

senses.definition: To follow or pursue; literally, to track a person's footsteps or trace.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence extends the idea of following a trace to pursuing something about which one lacks knowledge; the use is not limited to physical tracks.

senses.definition: To make a judgment by speculative tracing or conjecture.
senses.usage_conditions: In the interpretation of 17:36, the prohibition is explained as forbidding judgment by qiyāfah and conjecture. This is a Quran-specific figurative application of following or tracing, not a restriction on every use of the verb.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to follow after another; to send in succession.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction describes messengers being sent after an earlier messenger or group, with the Form II causative sense of making one follow behind another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The back of the neck; also the back or flat reverse surface of the hand, a knife, or a similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hand and knife applications are explicit extensions of the designation of a rear or back surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach or strike someone's nape.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression قَفَوْتُهُ, with the nape as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression عَيْنَاهُ فِي قَفَاهِ, to describe a fleeing person who keeps looking back in fear of pursuit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional idiomatic description rather than a general anatomical claim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Following a person's rear or track; figuratively, backbiting and tracing a person's faults.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative sense is presented as an euphemistic extension of following someone's rear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A craft or practice of conjectural tracing or inference.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its connection with اِقْتِفَاءٌ is reported as a reversal or metathesis, and the term is used in an explanation involving judgment by conjecture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The final part of a poetic line whose wording is observed and repeated across the poem; by extension, a verse or line, and then an ode or poem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meanings move from the ending of a line to the whole line and, by synecdoche and further extension, to a complete poem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food provided to someone as an act of personal attention or care.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term refers to food supplied for a person whom one attends to or looks after.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Direct tracking and following a trace are represented in the Form I pursuit sense.
Repeats the following-footsteps construction covered by the Form I pursuit sense.
The fleeing-person idiom is represented separately.
The extended back-surface applications are included with the anatomical meaning.
Pointer-only cross-reference with no supplied lexical definition.
The verse or single-line poetic use is represented under قَافِيَةٌ.
The extension to an ode or poem is included in the same poetic entry.

cautions: The public verb headwords are normalized citation forms; the Quranic occurrences themselves are the inflected forms تَقْفُ and وَقَفَّيْنَا.
The explanation linking قِيَافَةٌ with اِقْتِفَاءٌ is reported as a proposed reversal, so the derivational relationship should not be treated as certain.
